VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Duties for this position include, but are not limited to: The Registered Nurse (RN)-Ambulatory Surgery Registered Nurse is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to assigned patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting.

The nurse will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization consultation. Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others. Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence.

Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Shares educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Participates in activities and strategies to sustain an evidence-based-practice culture.

The Registered Nurse-Ambulatory Surgery Registered Nurse, provides pre-operative/procedural care, including (but not limited to) the nursing assessment of patients, consent, and H&P validations, the starting of intravenous fluids including venipuncture, assisting with peripheral nerve blocks, assuring all lab work and other pre-perative/procedural testing is completed and communicated to team members, confirms surgical sites are prepared and marked, and the administration of medications as ordered.

Provides clear and concise preoperative teaching and reviews discharge instructions to patients and families with written and verbal communication. The Ambulatory RN monitors post-operative patient's level of consciousness after the recovery of anesthesia/sedation. Closely observes signs of side effect of post residual anesthesia medications.

The Ambulatory RN maintains knowledge of current American Society of Peri anesthesia Nurses (ASPAN) standards, VHA Directive and service level standard operating procedures. The Ambulatory RN is responsible for ensuring comprehensive documentation of all phases of care and is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record.

Duties include but are not limited to: Responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising direct patient care. Assesses, plans, implements and evaluates care based on age-specific components.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient transition through the continuum of care, patient and family education, patient self-management after discharge, and supporting factors that impact customer satisfaction.

The Dedicated Charge Nurse, Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT) duties include, but are not limited to the following: The primary purpose of the dedicated charge registered nurse is to function as a frontline leader within Veterans Affairs North Texas Health Care System (VANTHCS) to maintain responsibility for the operations of the nursing unit.

The charge nurse demonstrates leadership in the application of the nursing process as it relates to clinical practice, teaching, leading staff, managing operational processes, and ensuring that patient needs are met.

He/she works collaboratively with the nurse manager in clinical and administrative duties such as delegating unit and patient care responsibilities, holding others accountable for providing safe patient care, providing input in monitoring and measuring staff performance, and collaborating with other health care and service providers to deliver safe and effective patient-centered care.

Additional charge nurse core functions include but are not limited to: Assisting the unit with meeting VANTHCS' organizational goals and values; setting the tone for the unit and establishing an appropriate work environment; considering patients' and family's needs; assessing the skills, personalities, and strengths of other staff; and providing and reevaluating a flexible staffing plan for shift needs.

The Charge Nurse is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising direct patient care. Assesses, plans, implements and evaluates care based on age-specific components.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient transition through the continuum of care, patient and family education, patient self-management after discharge, and supporting factors that impact customer satisfaction.

Considers all characteristics of the individual, including age and life stages, state of health, race and culture, clause, and previous experiences. Provides patient care and assessment, administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

Uses word processing software to execute several office automation functions such as storing and retrieving electronic documents and files; inserting and deleting text, formatting letters, reports, and memoranda; and transmitting and receiving email.

CTVHCS is in the process of making a cultural change, shifting from a disease-focused approach to a health and wellbeing approach, in order to implement the Whole Health System of Care. This is a VA-wide initiative to provide a comprehensive and systematic approach to improve healthcare delivery at all stages of Veteran care.

This entails moving from an episodic, "siloed" approach to an interdisciplinary, holistic approach, emphasizing self-care in the larger context of well-being.

All staff in this facility will be part of this process, shifting the focus from the question, "What's the matter with you?" to the question, "What matters to you, and how can we help you live your best life?" This strategy also involves integrating a full range of conventional approaches with Complementary and Integrative Health (CIH) approaches in order to optimize lifelong health and well-being, as defined by the Veteran, rather than narrowly focusing on disease management.

The Acute Psychiatry 94B, Nurse Manager (NM) is the designated first-line supervisory authority and is responsible and accountable for the 24/7 operation of their assigned units and provides coverage for other NMs as needed.

The NM is responsible and accountable for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance. They function as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team.

They enhance care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes. The NM engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

They adhere to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. They equip staff with tools for culturally competent care and promotes a culture of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

They cultivate alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. The NM contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care.

Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards. Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. They promote an inclusive workplace valuing diversity to achieve the organizations vision and mission.

The NM maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, Directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP). Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals.

Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes. Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Shares educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers.

Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Participates in activities and strategies to sustain an evidence-based practice culture. Upon assignment to this position, the incumbent's salary will include two additional steps for assignment to a Head Nurse/Nurse Manager position.

Duties and responsibilities of the HOME BASED PRIMARY CARE OUTPATIENT STAFF REGISTERED NURSE include, but are not limited to: Home Based Primary Care (HBPC) Outpatient Staff Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible and accountable for individual nursing practice and determines the appropriate delegation of tasks consistent with the nurse's obligation to provide optimal outpatient care.

This nurse provides direct Veteran care and care coordination, as it pertains, to Veterans and their care within the HBPC Program. Responsible for case management, assessment, triage, Veteran education, resource coordination, medication and treatment coordination, and care planning.

This nurse plans and delivers technically competent care in the home of Veterans with complex needs, including health promotion, health prevention, geriatric care, primary care, and palliative care. Utilizes interventions, which maximize health capabilities and reduces unnecessary urgent care and emergency room visits, per Veteran's goals of care.

Makes home visits to Veterans in the program. The focus is on individual growth and development in HBPC nursing practice with increased levels of self direction. Seeks guidance on how to improve care provided to patients and families.

Delegates elements of care to the appropriate individual based upon assessed needs, condition, and safety of the patient. The nurse brings HBPC principles and theory with limited application of critical thinking skills.

Responsible for participating within unit based and/or organizational level Shared Governance councils, utilizing clinical expertise, evidence-based practice, and knowledge to assist with finding solutions to problems or issues to improve the quality care provided to our veterans.

Garland Dermatology Specialty Clinic Float RN is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based specialty care to patients and serves as a member of the interdisciplinary team to promote quality, safe, and patient-centered care.

The RN provides patient care, care coordination, health promotion, health education, and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management. This position serves as a member of the Garland Specialty Care Float Pool and provides nursing support across specialty care outpatient clinics based on patient care and staffing needs.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Responsible and accountable for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care.

Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates care using the nursing process and administers medications and procedures in accordance with established policies and guidelines. Provides patient care, care coordination, health promotion, health education, and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management.

Collaborates with members of the interdisciplinary team to influence care outcomes and ensure achievement of the plan of care. Assists in directing nursing education, orientation, competencies, quality improvement activities, and outcomes utilization, as appropriate to the clinic setting.

Partners with patients, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team to promote effective and safe transitions across the health care continuum, including the Veteran's goals of care.

Provides oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the clinic setting, and delegates elements of care based on assessed patient needs, condition, and safety.

Evaluates practice based on best evidence and participates in activities and strategies that support an evidence-based practice culture and performance improvement activities.

Supports a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of health care professionals through knowledge sharing, mentoring, coaching, and constructive feedback.

Demonstrates leadership, critical thinking, sound clinical judgment, and effective communication in managing patient care and competing priorities within the specialty care setting.

Provides specialty care nursing support across multiple outpatient specialty clinics to ensure continuity of care, support staffing coverage, and meet patient care needs in areas requiring additional nursing resources.

Die Station Mistral ist ein geschützter Ort mit einer klaren Tagesstruktur für Kinder zwischen 6 und 12 Jahren, die aufgrund psychischer Belastungen oder akuter Krisen intensive kinderpsychiatrische Unterstützung ötigen. Gemeinsam mit den Kindern und ihren Familien schaffen wir einen Rahmen, in dem Sicherheit, Vertrauen und neue Perspektiven entstehen können.
Wir stehen Kindern und Jugendlichen in akuten Krisensituationen zur Seite, geben Halt und Orientierung und setzen auf reflektiertes, ruhiges Handeln, um gemeinsam tragfähige Lösungen zu entwickeln.
Unser pädagogisch\-therapeutisches Milieu verbindet psychodynamische, verhaltenstherapeutische und systemische Ansätze. Wir arbeiten eng mit der Klinikschule, den Familien und einem multiprofessionellen Team zusammen, um Entwicklung Schritt für Schritt zu ermöglichen.

Du begleitest Kinder im pädagogisch\-therapeutischen Milieu und unterstützt sie dabei, ihre Gefühle besser wahrzunehmen, neue Bewältigungsstrategien zu entwickeln und ihren Therapieprozess aktiv mitzugestalten
Du begleitest Kinder in akuten Krisensituationen, stellst Sicherheit her, gibst Orientierung und unterstützt das Team, die Krise fachlich zu klären
Du trägst Mitverantwortung bei der Gestaltung und Leitung von Gruppentherapien
Du arbeitest als Bezugsperson eng mit Fachpersonen aus Pädagogik, Psychologie, Medizin und Therapie zusammen
Du bringst deine fachliche Perspektive in den diagnostischen Prozess ein und hilfst mit, ein gemeinsames Fallverständnis zu entwickeln
Du arbeitest im Schichtbetrieb ohne Nachtdienste
Du übernimmst Verantwortung für dokumentierte Zielklärungen und die Umsetzung der therapeutischen Schritte im Alltag
Du gestaltest die Zusammenarbeit mit Eltern und Sorgeberechtigten konstruktiv und wertschätzend
Du unterstützt neue Fachpersonen in der Praxisausbildung und begleitest sie im Alltag
Du trägst zur Weiterentwicklung unserer pädagogischen Qualität und zur Einhaltung der Leistungsziele der Klinik bei

Du verfügst über eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung in Sozialpädagogik HF / FH oder als Pflegefachperson HF/FH und bringst idealerweise Erfahrung in der Arbeit mit Kindern und Jugendlichen mit
Du bringst die nötige Qualifikation für die Praxisausbildung mit oder bist bereit, einen Fachkurs zu absolvieren
Du hast Freude an Beziehungsgestaltung, Alltagsstruktur und der Arbeit mit Familien
Du hast die Fähigkeit, dein Handeln zu reflektieren und in Krisensituationen ruhig und lösungsorientiert zu bleiben

Description de l'entreprise
Ancrée dans le panorama de la Riviera depuis 1905, la Clinique Valmont offre des séjours de réadaptation personnalisés pour les personnes présentant des atteintes neurologiques, orthopédiques et du dos, dans un cadre exceptionnel, face au Lac Léman et aux Alpes.

Aujourd'hui, elle est devenue un établissement phare dans la réadaptation, de par son efficience thérapeutique inégalée, ses équipes compétentes et son plateau technique de pointe.

En effet, les médecins en réadaptation collaborent avec une équipe d'experts multidisciplinaires, composée de physiothérapeutes, ergothérapeutes, neuropsychologues, logopédistes, maîtres de sport et diététicienne. En 2006, la clinique a rejoint Swiss Medical Network, l'un des deux principaux groupes suisses de cliniques privées.
Description du poste
En tant qu'ICUS, vous assurez un rôle clé dans l'organisation et le pilotage des activités de soins au sein de la clinique de réadaptation.

Participez activement à la gestion de l'équipe soignante (planification, encadrement, accompagnement des collaborateurs, gestion des priorités).
Veillez à la fluidité, à la qualité et à la fiabilité des informations transmises au sein de l'établissement et entre les différents acteurs de la prise en charge.
Garantissez l'efficience de la prise en charge des patients, en assurant une organisation optimale des ressources et une répartition adéquate de la charge de travail.
Assurez la qualité et la sécurité des soins, dans le respect des normes, protocoles et exigences institutionnelles.
Contribuez au développement, à l'optimisation et à l'harmonisation des processus de soins.
Participez à la mise en place, à l'évaluation et au suivi des protocoles de réadaptation, en collaboration avec les équipes pluridisciplinaires.
Soutenez les équipes sur le terrain et intervenez dans les situations complexes.
Favorisez un climat de travail positif et une dynamique d'équipe constructive.

This Registered Nurse- Operating Room is located in the Nursing, Perioperative Service at the Manchester VA location. This position is full-time at 40 hours per week.

Duties are Included but are not limited to: Independently circulate a wide range of surgical procedures, ensuring adherence to sterile technique, patient safety standards, surgical time-outs, accurate documentation, and effective coordination among the interdisciplinary perioperative team throughout all phases of care according to National and local VA directives.

Perform scrub nurse responsibilities for diverse surgical specialties by maintaining sterile fields, preparing and handling surgical instruments and supplies, anticipating surgeon needs, and supporting safe, efficient intraoperative patient care. Manage OR equipment as it applies to the surgical procedure.

Interview the patient and review the preoperative assessment, check chart for required documentation: history and physical examination, consents, day of surgery note, correct surgical site, laboratory tests results, lab values, allergies, and NPO status. Assist anesthesia provider with induction within Nursing Scope of Practice.

Review surgeon's preference card and prepare the OR for the surgery. Ensure availability of instruments, equipment, sterile supplies, and implants. Ensure proper patient positioning for various surgical procedures. Complete documentation on OR record using the electronic health record (Vista/CPRS).

Perform surgical counts of instruments, sharps, sponges, and miscellaneous items with the scrub person per policy. Work collaboratively with all levels of health care professional and support staff to facilitate positive patient care outcomes.

Compliance with PPE, precautions, and Infection Control Guidelines Skills in time management, priority setting, assessment and urgent intervention are essential to develop. Demonstrate leadership by active participation in charge nurse duties and unit/hospital committees. Offer staffing support to PACU and surgical clinics.

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life.

More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between.

Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.
Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .
The Opportunity
Carrot is expanding its telemedicine clinic with a network of part-time to full-time, fully remote Registered Nurses who deliver evidence-based virtual care to members across all U.S. states. As an RN in this network, you are often the first clinical touchpoint for members navigating fertility, menopause, hormonal, and metabolic health journeys, providing triage, education, care coordination, and documentation that shape the entire care experience.
All work in this role is performed within RN scope of practice. RNs provide triage, education, care coordination, and documentation; they do not diagnose, do not prescribe, and do not independently modify a treatment plan. Anything requiring clinical judgment beyond RN scope is routed to a physician, so sound escalation judgment is central to the role.
This is a contractor engagement of approximately 20-40 hours per week, with scheduled shifts within the Monday-Friday, 8:00a-6:00p CST coverage window.
What You’ll Own

Serve as the first clinical reviewer of inbound member messages, triaging for urgency, escalating to a physician when needed, and routing non-clinical threads to the appropriate support team.
Deliver member education on menopause staging, hormone therapy, preconception health, metabolic health, and medication administration.
Review and triage incoming lab results, escalate critical findings per protocol, retrieve outside records, and coordinate specialist referrals.
Manage pharmacy callbacks and prior authorizations in coordination with the care team.
Document all clinically relevant interactions same-day, create tracked internal tasks with named owners, and follow established escalation pathways.
Maintain active NLC multi-state licensure, complete required credentialing and onboarding, and adhere to HIPAA, continuing education, and liability coverage requirements.
Contribute to chart audits and clinical protocol feedback as the telemedicine program scales.
What Success Looks Like

s.h: In your first 12–18 months, you will have
s.t:
Established a consistent record of accurate, protocol-aligned triage with appropriate physician escalation and no missed critical lab values.
Maintained same-day documentation and timely lab follow-up, with no outstanding credentialing or compliance gaps.
Delivered high-quality member education across menopause, preconception, hormone therapy, and metabolic health topics, reflected in strong member experience results.
Managed care coordination workflows reliably within your coverage window, including referrals, records retrieval, prior authorizations, and pharmacy callbacks.
Contributed to chart audits, protocol feedback, and quality improvement as the telemedicine program scales.

An active, unrestricted RN license with NLC (Nurse Licensure Compact) multi-state privileges, in good standing, plus an ADN or BSN from an accredited program (BSN preferred).
A minimum of 3 years of active RN clinical experience, with meaningful experience in women's health, reproductive health, OB/GYN, fertility, endocrinology, or menopause care.
Demonstrated nurse triage experience, including assessing urgency, applying protocol, escalating appropriately, and recognizing critical lab values.
A clear understanding of RN scope of practice and sound judgment about when to escalate.
Strong written communication for asynchronous messaging and a strong phone presence for symptom assessment and instruction.
Proficiency with EHR and telehealth systems, secure messaging, and e-fax workflows.
Familiarity with HIPAA and applicable telemedicine privacy, security, and regulatory requirements.
The ability to commit to scheduled shifts within the Monday-Friday, 8:00a-6:00p CST coverage window, with a HIPAA-compliant, private home workspace and reliable internet.

s.h: While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring
s.t:
Experience in a dedicated menopause clinic, fertility center, REI practice, or comparable specialty program.
Familiarity with preconception and fertility workup, including AMH and hormone panels, ovulation tracking, and cycle-monitoring labs.
Hormone therapy education experience, including prior authorization workflows.
Experience supporting members on anti-obesity medications, including GLP-1 receptor agonists.
Prior experience in digital health, health benefits, or multi-state telemedicine environments.
Experience contributing to clinical protocol development, quality improvement, or member-facing clinical content.
Experience supporting diverse and historically underserved populations, including LGBTQ+ and gender-diverse individuals.
Relevant certification (e.g., MSCP through The Menopause Society, RNC-OB) and/or fluency in an additional language.
